subject.title: Runtime context carrier positioned AFTER user message causes severe model confusion and reasoning token waste

question: Should OpenClaw keep the documented prompt-cache-first tail placement, or change the core default after provider evidence shows that user-role carrier ordering harms reasoning quality or delivery reliability?
rationale: The code intentionally optimizes cache-prefix reuse, while the report asks to trade that invariant for model-behavior quality; source inspection alone cannot set the acceptable cross-provider tradeoff.

options.title: Measure then change the default if warranted
options.body: Run a bounded provider matrix against current main and switch the canonical placement only if it materially improves behavior without unacceptable cache or delivery regressions.

options.title: Keep the cache-first placement
options.body: Retain tail placement and close only after evidence shows the observed model behavior is provider-specific or not reproducible.

options.title: Adopt a structured-context redesign
options.body: Design a role-preserving carrier path if provider contracts make either same-role ordering unacceptable.

recommendation.title: Measure then change the default if warranted
recommendation.body: Run a bounded provider matrix against current main and switch the canonical placement only if it materially improves behavior without unacceptable cache or delivery regressions.

likelyOwner.reason: No individual ownership attribution was supportable from the available feature-history evidence.
